_comment: The whole schedule lives here. Editing this file is how the music changes. Nothing in the code knows about a store, a time or a playlist name.

stores.name: Home (TV Room + 4)

slots.name: Evening
slots._pool_note: Chosen by Andrew 2026-09-10. All seven checked live on the system that day: every one is a Spotify playlist, so all of them shuffle and crossfade. Seven dealt one a night means a week before any repeats.

slots.name: Night
slots._pool_note: Andrew added 'Goodnight Mix' to the home system on 2026-09-10 and asked for it in place of 'AMBIENT CALM', which was never saved there. Checked live that day: it exists and is a Spotify track list, unlike the other two here which are Calm Radio streams, so shuffle, repeat and crossfade apply to it on the nights it is dealt. It keeps the volume 15 Andrew set for the entry it replaces, quieter than the slot's 18.

stores._home_comment: Daytime must be Calm Radio only. Spotify plays in one place at a time, and during the day Andrew is out and using Spotify himself, so a scheduled job on Spotify would cut him off. His Calm Radio stations are the ones named in capitals. Evening and night are unrestricted because he is home and not playing Spotify elsewhere. From midnight the music stops until the nine in the morning start, asked for 2026-09-06.
stores._leave_off_note: Asked for 2026-09-07. If Andrew stops the music himself, it stays stopped. It starts again on its own at the next change of slot, which at home means nine in the morning, six in the evening or eleven at night. Shops deliberately do not have this: a silent room during service is a fault, not a choice.
stores._day_rules_note: Set 2026-09-10 by Andrew. Sunroom silent in the daytime on Tue, Wed and Thu. TV Room silent EVERY evening, all seven nights. Weekends start at 10:00 rather than 09:00; Mon and Fri and the weekend play in every room. Silent means volume 0 with the speaker still in the group, never ungrouped: that is the decision recorded on 2026-09-06, because splitting and rejoining needs the software to remember what it undid and a failure leaves the house split until someone notices. Ceilings are Andrew's: Sunroom 20, TV Room 20, Dressing Room 25, Bedroom 25, Kitchen 28. Evenings sit below the ceiling in the same proportion they always did.
stores._christmas_note: Andrew's instruction 2026-09-10: treat home the same as the shops, 50/50, not pure Christmas. Kept as home's OWN holiday rather than added to the shared block, because two tests exist specifically to stop a shop rule following home around, and they were right. ⚠️ 'December Evening 50-50 (home)' DOES NOT EXIST YET. The mixing lives in the Spotify playlist, never in the software, so it has to be built half Christmas half not, and saved as a favourite on the home system before December. The thirteen pure Christmas playlists on that system are deliberately NOT scheduled: rule 2 of 2026-09-05 forbids a Christmas playlist running on its own, and Andrew has now extended that rule to home.

stores.name: West Harlem, 3600 Broadway
stores._note: Switched on 2026-09-09, the day of the flagship visit, and proven the same afternoon: run 241 found it playing its scheduled playlist, already correct, and eased a drifted volume back down. Lives under contact@thehandpullednoodle.com, a different Sonos account from the other two stores, authorised that day via connect.py. Favourites verified: 67 saved. FOH Jazz exists here only as 'FOH Jazz (From Joel)', so this store's slots avoid that name. Andrew confirmed the floor pattern matches Central Harlem, quiet till about 12:30, so the slots below mirror that shape, built only from names in the verified 67.
stores._volume_note: ⚠️ TEMPORARY, set 2026-09-10. Flat 28 at every hour because THE SPEAKER IS FAULTY: the bass blows when it is driven louder. First capped at 32 the same afternoon and that was still too loud, so 28. This is a hardware limit, not a taste choice: do not raise it for a busier room. WHEN THE NEW SONOS IS FITTED, two things change together. Restore the curve heard in the room that morning: 33 soft open, 39 lunch, 33 dead stretch, 37 early evening, 40 dinner peak, 35 last service, ceiling 40. And the speaker serial changes, so SONOS_SPEAKER_WEST_HARLEM must be updated too or the group lookup silently stops protecting this store.

stores.name: Central Harlem, 370 Malcolm X (one speaker, Dining Room)
stores._note: LABEL CORRECTED 2026-09-09 evening: this entry said two speakers for days, but the speaker roll call showed the system holds exactly one, named Dining Room, and Andrew confirmed from the floor that the single speaker IS Central Harlem. The morning's wizard therefore verified the right system all along. Same day, earlier: enabled in the morning without its keys in secure storage, so runs silently skipped it until the keys went in that afternoon. Also that day: the group id from Sunday died when Andrew power-cycled the speaker during the wifi fix, because Sonos mints a new group id when a group re-forms; the fresh id was read with connect.py and pasted into secure storage by Andrew. Lesson, twice over: enabled means scheduled, keys mean reachable, and any power cycle can kill a stored group id, so a 410 RESOURCE_GONE after a store visit means re-read the group id, not much else. A build is queued to look the group up fresh by name each run so this stops being manual. Slots: Andrew corrected the shared timetable from the floor, near empty at 11:30, real rush 12:30 to 2, so the day opens chill. Pools deal one playlist per day per slot. Every name below was verified saved on this system 2026-09-09. FOH Jazz and Feel Good Jazz were deliberately skipped and are not referenced here.

slots.name: Lunch rush
playlist_pool: The Best Upbeat Instrumental Jazz Collection

stores._volume_note: Set 2026-09-10 by Andrew: base 30, ceiling 38. The existing shape is kept, so the quiet slots sit at the base and the dinner peak reaches the ceiling. One speaker, so one level.

stores.name: Hell's Kitchen, 354 West 44th (left and right pair)
stores._note: IDENTITY CORRECTED 2026-09-09 evening. This store's system is the two-speaker pair, Dining Room Left Speaker and Dining Room Right Speaker, under contact@thenoodle.nyc, confirmed by Andrew from the speaker roll call. These files had been calling that pair 'Central Harlem's lone One SL' since at least 2026-09-07, and a central-harlem-b entry existed for it; that entry is deleted, this note is its grave marker. The 2026-09-08 shop-visit note said the speaker was renamed Dining Room THPN-HK; no speaker by that name exists on the account now, so the rename did not stick. Its favourites were confirmed 2026-09-09 to include every shared-timetable name, Jazz Trumpet, Instrumental Jazz Standards, FOH Jazz, Jazz Classics Blue Note Edition and Feel Good Jazz, so the earlier worry about missing names is resolved. OPEN ISSUE: something on this system keeps restarting its old favourites between runs, seen at 14:30, 14:45, 15:00 on 2026-09-09, each time corrected by the schedule; nobody touches the speakers by hand, so the prime suspect is old Sonos alarms on this system, which can only be deleted from the app on the shop's own wifi. Delete every alarm there on the next Hell's Kitchen visit. Until then the quarter-hourly repair holds the line. Second open question: the One SL bought in February is now unaccounted for; it may be one of this pair or sitting unregistered somewhere.
stores._note_2: Still on the shared timetable below. Andrew's quiet-till-12:30 floor pattern held at both Harlem stores and likely holds here; check against the Toast busy-hours analysis before giving this store its own slots.
stores._volume_note: Set 2026-09-10 by Andrew. Per speaker, because the right speaker is the walled-off corner and runs softer: right 28 to 35, left 30 to 38, both moving together across the shared slot shape. ⚠️ This REPLACES the balance that was set by hand in the Sonos app on 2026-09-08 (left 33, right 25). The software now sets both absolutely, so changing the corner balance means changing these numbers, not the app.

_slots_comment: All three stores run the same hours, confirmed 2026-09-05. Times are 24 hour. Music runs 11:30 to 23:00; outside those hours nothing plays. Central Harlem and West Harlem carry their own slots on their store entries; Andrew's 2026-09-09 floor observation, empty at 11:30 and rush 12:30 to 2, is confirmed for both Harlem stores and should be checked for Hell's Kitchen against the Toast busy-hours analysis, spec in run-the-house docs.
_volume_comment: Volumes are a starting guess, not Andrew's current settings. He sets these per alarm today and those numbers should replace these.
_seasons_comment: A season swaps the playlist for named slots. Anything not listed keeps its default. Seasonal change should be felt and not noticed.

autumn._note: Set 2026-09-10, and moved the same day: Andrew said September is too early, so autumn starts 1 October rather than 1 September. September now falls in no season at all, which simply means the default playlists, and that is the intent. Andrew's seven evening playlists PLUS three autumn ones, dealt as one deck of ten. Blended rather than replaced, because this document's own rule is that a seasonal change should be felt and not noticed: three in ten evenings is felt. Only home has a slot called 'Evening', so this touches nothing in the shops. 'Fall Asleep Instantly' is deliberately excluded: it is a sleep playlist whose name merely begins with the word.

_holidays_comment: Holidays outrank seasons, which outrank the default. Christmas never starts before the first week of December, and the 50/50 mix of Christmas and non-Christmas tracks is built into the playlist itself, not by the software. Holiday overrides name slots; Central Harlem's and West Harlem's own slot names include the same 'Lunch rush', 'Dead stretch', 'Early evening', 'Dinner peak' and 'Last service', so the December and holiday overrides still land there. The 'Soft open' slot has no override and stays chill in December, which is right.
_rules_comment: Standing rules, kept here so they are visible to anyone editing this file. Never sad, never sombre, always positive. Five items of taste only: instrumental jazz, big band, classic jazz vocals. Nothing experimental. The music is never handed to staff.
